problem_text:
A logistics firm must coordinate a supply circuit through six regional depots, each positioned at distinct geographical points:
Depot Alpha: situated at grid reference (5,139)
Depot Beta: situated at grid reference (108,158)
Depot Gamma: situated at grid reference (25,66)
Depot Delta: situated at grid reference (17,56)
Depot Epsilon: situated at grid reference (18,165)
Depot Zeta: situated at grid reference (77,89)

The travel distances between depots, measured in kilometers, are precisely defined:
Alpha to Gamma: 75.7 km
Alpha to Delta: 83.9 km
Alpha to Epsilon: 29.1 km
Alpha to Zeta: 87.7 km
Beta to Gamma: 123.9 km
Beta to Delta: 136.7 km
Beta to Epsilon: 90.3 km
Beta to Zeta: 75.6 km
Gamma to Delta: 12.8 km
Gamma to Epsilon: 99.2 km
Gamma to Zeta: 56.9 km
Delta to Epsilon: 109.0 km
Delta to Zeta: 68.5 km
Epsilon to Zeta: 96.2 km

Direct transit between Depot Alpha and Depot Beta is not permitted due to infrastructural constraints.
Furthermore, the circuit must incorporate exactly one of the following two critical links: the route connecting Depot Beta and Depot Gamma, or the route connecting Depot Gamma and Depot Delta.

The objective is to determine the minimal total travel distance for a closed loop that visits every depot precisely one time, commencing and concluding at the same initial depot.
